service.name: Wedding music in Fort Collins
service.serviceType: Live music for weddings in Fort Collins: ceremony guitarist, cocktail hour duo, band and DJ
service.description: Live wedding music in Fort Collins and northern Colorado: an acoustic, jazz or Spanish guitarist for a ceremony in the foothills, on a ranch or in the Poudre canyon, a jazz or acoustic duo for an Old Town cocktail hour, a band or the DJ for a ballroom or barn reception, on one contract with sound included and one flat Front Range travel line.

faqs.q: Do you play weddings in Fort Collins?
faqs.a: Yes, the whole day or any one part of it. Fort Collins is about an hour up I-25 from Denver, so the music is quoted at the fee a Denver wedding sees plus one flat Front Range travel line, with no lodging. Every size arrives with sound, setup and pack-down, a certificate of insurance and a W-9. Signet Artists books Fort Collins weddings from Denver.

faqs.q: What does the Fort Collins travel line cover?
faqs.a: The drive up I-25 and back for the musicians and the gear, as one flat line, the same line a Colorado Springs or Boulder date carries. A ceremony up the Poudre canyon adds the canyon road and a drop in cell coverage to the plan rather than to the price, so setup is timed with the venue and the musicians leave early.

faqs.q: Is a duo enough for a taproom or courtyard reception in Old Town?
faqs.a: For the cocktail hour and dinner, yes. A jazz or acoustic duo, in a corner of about 8 by 6 feet on one circuit, is the size an Old Town courtyard or a taproom's event space books. When the same night wants a floor, a trio fills one without a stage and the DJ takes the same sound system when the band is done.

faqs.q: How much setup time does it need?
faqs.a: Setup runs 45 to 60 minutes for a solo, a duo or a trio and 90 for a quartet, through whichever door the venue prefers. Parking in Old Town is the question to settle with the venue early.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book wedding musicians in Fort Collins?
faqs.a: The Old Town hotels and the ranch venues book their summer and fall Saturdays a year or more out, and the university's calendar fills the hotels on some weekends, so the venue and the date come first and the music right after. Tell us the date and we'll come back quickly with an answer and a price.
